name: sylius
_readme: Sylius as migration TARGET (API Platform REST/JSON-LD, Twig storefront or headless) and as SOURCE (a Symfony application: project code under src/, Sylius bundles under vendor/sylius). Seed from general Symfony/Sylius knowledge; everything in research-seed.md is a hypothesis until verified with a docs.sylius.com / sylius.com URL and a date. Note the honest headline: Sylius core ships no CMS. No adapter.py yet: a source scan needs one.

as_source.language_stack: PHP 8.x / Symfony 6 or 7, Doctrine ORM, MySQL or PostgreSQL; API Platform for the API layer
as_source.default_frontend: Twig storefront (Bootstrap-based; the 2.x storefront is rebuilt around Twig Hooks) or headless on the API
do_not_run: yarn install / yarn build / bin/console assets:install (asset build)
composer install / update against the client repository

snippets.version_markers: composer.lock -> locked version of sylius/sylius (plus sylius/plus, sylius/*-plugin and any BitBag/community plugin), and of symfony/framework-bundle and doctrine/orm; composer.json require constraints are the intent, the lock file is the fact; config/bundles.php shows which bundles the application really loads; a plugin's own composer.json require on sylius/sylius gives its compatibility window. Also check migrations/Version*.php timestamps for how recently the schema moved, and symfony.lock / .env for the framework baseline. Report the Sylius minor AND the Symfony major - a Sylius upgrade is usually a Symfony upgrade too.
snippets.active_units_config: AUTHORITATIVE for bundle activation: config/bundles.php - a bundle that exists under src/ or in vendor but is not listed there is DEAD and its services are never loaded (unless another loaded bundle registers them). Also read: config/packages/*.yaml (per-bundle configuration and Sylius resource overrides, env-specific subfolders dev/prod/test), config/services.yaml (project service wiring and autoconfiguration excludes), config/routes/*.yaml plus config/routes.yaml (which controllers are reachable at all - an unrouted controller is dead), and .env/.env.local feature switches. Channel-level behaviour (which channel is enabled, its theme, its locales, currencies, payment and shipping methods) is DATABASE data, not repository configuration - say so before calling a feature active or inactive.
snippets.package_sources: composer.json require of the project root (sylius/sylius, sylius/*-plugin, sylius/plus, bitbag/*-plugin, other community plugins, symfony/*, doctrine/*) and composer.lock for resolved versions; per-bundle composer.json under src/ if the project splits its own code into packages; package.json / yarn.lock for the storefront and admin assets (Sylius ships Webpack Encore / Gulp asset pipelines depending on the version).
snippets.override_mechanisms: overridden = the standard behaviour is replaced: Sylius RESOURCE overriding (`sylius_<bundle>: resources: <resource>: classes: model|controller|factory|repository|form` in config/packages/_sylius.yaml or a dedicated file) - this is the sanctioned way to swap a model, factory, repository or form and is the first thing to look for; a service definition re-declaring an existing Sylius service id; a DI decorator (`decorates:` or #[AsDecorator]) that changes behaviour rather than adding to it; a full Twig template override under templates/bundles/SyliusShopBundle|SyliusAdminBundle/** (same relative path hides the Sylius template); a replaced grid definition (sylius_grid configuration for an admin grid); a replaced state-machine callback. extended = added without replacing: an event subscriber on Sylius events (sylius.order.pre_complete, sylius.cart.post_add, kernel events, Doctrine lifecycle events), a Doctrine entity extending a Sylius model class with added fields plus a resource-class override that only points to the subclass, Twig Hooks (2.x - insertion points that add blocks without hiding templates), a new API Platform resource or operation, a new grid, a new state-machine transition, a custom form extension (`FormTypeExtension` on a Sylius form). shadowed / core-patch = a patched file under vendor/sylius or a project class declared inside the Sylius\ namespace - highest risk, name the file. Distinguish full Twig override from Twig Hooks in every finding: on 2.x the hook is the maintainable variant and the override is upgrade debt.
snippets.schema_sources: Doctrine entities under src/Entity (or src/<Bundle>/Entity) plus their mapping: PHP attributes on the class, or XML/YAML under Resources/config/doctrine/*.orm.xml - an entity extending a Sylius model with added fields is a schema EXTENSION of the Sylius table (single table, added columns), a standalone entity is a new table: say which; migrations under migrations/Version*.php (read up() and down(), note destructive steps and raw SQL); the resource configuration that binds the entity class to the Sylius resource; and translation entities (Sylius uses *Translation classes for localised fields - a new translatable field means two tables).
snippets.workflow_sources: state machines are the order lifecycle: winzou_state_machine configuration (config/packages/_sylius.yaml or winzou_state_machine.yaml) for sylius_order_checkout, sylius_order, sylius_order_payment, sylius_order_shipping, sylius_payment, sylius_shipment, sylius_product_review - on newer versions the Symfony Workflow component may be configured instead; read the graph's states, transitions and callbacks (callbacks are where custom logic hangs). Also: Symfony Messenger buses and handlers (config/packages/messenger.yaml), Sylius promotion rules/actions and shipping-method rules registered as tagged services, and scheduled commands (sylius:cancel-unpaid-orders and project cron entries).
snippets.data_script_sources: sylius:fixtures suites (config/packages/_sylius.yaml `sylius_fixtures:` or fixtures/*.yaml) and custom Fixture/DataFixture classes, plus any project import command (Symfony console command reading CSV/XML), Doctrine migrations that INSERT configuration data (payment/shipping methods, channels, locales - very common and easy to miss), and API-based import scripts against /api/v2/admin/*. Note which of these are idempotent.
snippets.read_order: composer.json + composer.lock, config/bundles.php, config/packages/**/*.yaml (especially _sylius.yaml and any sylius_* resource override), config/services.yaml, config/routes*.yaml, then per bundle/module: Entity classes and Doctrine mapping, migrations/, Resources/config/services.xml, controllers and API Platform resource configuration, forms and form extensions, grids, state-machine configuration and callbacks, templates/bundles/** (full overrides) and Twig hook configuration, event subscribers, Messenger handlers, fixtures, tests last (intent only). Before asserting behaviour, check config/bundles.php and the routing - and remember that channel/payment/shipping configuration lives in the database.
snippets.hosting_constraints: Sylius is a plain Symfony application with no managed offering from the vendor: hosting is self-managed (any PHP hosting, or a PaaS such as Platform.sh) and everything operational is the project's own responsibility - MySQL/PostgreSQL, cron (sylius:cancel-unpaid-orders and project jobs), Messenger workers as long-running processes, asset builds at deploy time, Elasticsearch/Algolia if search was added. Constraints to state when moving TO a container platform: media is stored on the local filesystem by default (public/media) and needs a Flysystem adapter for object storage; the cache and session storage must move out of the filesystem; `var/log` and file-based locks do not survive multiple instances. There is no vendor SaaS to fall back to, so a 'managed' requirement is a platform mismatch, not a configuration task.
snippets.api_families_hint: API Platform REST/JSON-LD under /api/v2/shop and /api/v2/admin - see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families

as_target.default_frontend: Twig storefront (2.x rebuilt around Twig Hooks) or headless on the API Platform API

snippets.critic2_persona: senior Symfony/Sylius solution architect who has delivered several Sylius projects, knows the resource-override and Twig-Hook extension model, and is precise about what is Sylius Community, what needs Sylius Plus or the B2B Suite, what is a community plugin and what is simply project code to be written
snippets.docs_domains: docs.sylius.com (developer documentation: customization guide - the resource/model/factory/repository/form override mechanics, API Platform integration, state machines, grids, Twig Hooks, upgrade guides per version), api.sylius.com (API reference), github.com/Sylius/Sylius releases and UPGRADE-*.md (the authoritative deprecation and breaking-change record), sylius.com for Plus / B2B Suite scope and pricing, plus the plugin's own repository for any community plugin (BitBag and others). Always name the Sylius minor AND the Symfony major, and say whether a capability is core, Plus, a plugin, or project code.
snippets.best_practice: use the sanctioned override chain instead of inheritance tricks: resource configuration to swap model/factory/repository/form, event subscribers and Twig Hooks to add behaviour, DI decoration where a service must be wrapped; never patch vendor/sylius; keep domain logic in services behind interfaces (the codebase's own standard is SOLID plus BDD coverage - match it or the argument for choosing Sylius disappears); model schema changes as Doctrine migrations with a reversible down(); keep the order lifecycle in the state machine and hang custom logic on callbacks rather than in controllers; expose everything a frontend needs as an API Platform operation so the Twig storefront and a headless frontend stay interchangeable; budget explicitly for the features Sylius does not ship, above all content management.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: Sylius minor and Symfony major, deprecations from UPGRADE-*.md, and whether the required capability is core, Sylius Plus, B2B Suite, a community plugin (name it and its maintenance state) or project code. D2: is the named counterpart a real Sylius service/resource/state-machine graph, and is the extension mechanism the sanctioned one (resource override / hook / subscriber) rather than a template override or a patch. D3: does Sylius really cover the requirement out of the box - Sylius is a framework, so 'coverable with development' must never be scored as covered-standard; name the plugin or the development effort. D4: exact /api/v2/shop and /api/v2/admin resource paths and whether the operation exists for that resource, plus the content question - there is no core CMS, so every content requirement needs a named plugin or an external CMS.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: content management of any depth (no CMS in core - landing pages, editorial content, campaign pages and content versioning all need a plugin or a headless CMS); B2B breadth (organisations, roles, budgets, approvals, quotes) which sits in Sylius Plus / the B2B Suite or in custom code; admin depth for merchandising, marketing and reporting compared with all-in-one platforms; search and merchandising beyond a basic Doctrine/Elasticsearch setup; customer-specific and contract pricing driven by an ERP; configurable products and CPQ; subscriptions; loyalty; multi-warehouse inventory and returns handling; tax and compliance specifics; and anything a stakeholder assumes is 'standard shop functionality' because they came from an all-in-one platform.
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: Sylius core ships no CMS, so the content workstream must be decided before anything else (community CMS plugin vs. headless CMS vs. custom - each changes the frontend architecture); the ecosystem is small, so plugin maintenance state and Sylius-version compatibility are project risks, not details; B2B features are Plus/B2B Suite or custom, and Plus is a paid license with its own feature boundary; nothing is turnkey - the platform requires development to launch, so a fast-launch or low-budget requirement is a platform mismatch; hosting and operations are entirely self-managed with no vendor SaaS; API Platform coverage must be checked operation by operation (a resource existing does not mean the operation you need exists); the Twig storefront and a headless frontend are different projects - a template-heavy source system does not port; and migrating channel/payment/shipping/promotion configuration is database work because it does not live in the repository.
snippets.content_model_notes: Sylius core ships NO CMS: there is no page, block or content entity in Sylius Standard, and no page builder. This is the single most important content fact about the platform and must be stated in every assessment. What core offers instead is content-BEARING commerce data: Taxons (categories with translated name, description, slug and images), product translations and product attributes, product images and associations, and Channel-level settings (theme, hostname, contact details, menu taxon). Editorial content is therefore one of three decisions: (1) a community CMS plugin - the BitBag CMS plugin family (Page, Block, Media, Section, FAQ) is the common choice, which makes the project dependent on a third-party plugin's Sylius-version compatibility; (2) a headless CMS (Contentful, Strapi, Storyblok) composed in the frontend, which is the cleanest option for a headless build but adds a second system and license; (3) custom entities plus admin grids, which is honest but is development effort in every estimate. Rendering: the Twig storefront is customised through template overrides and, on 2.x, Twig Hooks (insertion points that add content without hiding templates - prefer them); a headless frontend renders nothing automatically and must implement every component itself. Never score a content requirement as covered-standard on Sylius.
